clearing_status.fact: On Feb 25, 2025, the SEC issued Exchange Act Release No. 34-102487 formally extending compliance dates by one year to Dec 31, 2026 (cash) and Jun 30, 2027 (repo). As of the SEC's Aug 7, 2026 implementation update, those dates remain in force with no second extension, but SIFMA and IIB exemptive-relief requests published Apr 17, 2026 remain pending. Source: sec.gov press release 2025-43 (Feb 25, 2025) and sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/uyeda-...august-2026 (Aug 7, 2026).
clearing_status.rationale: The rubric scores 1 ('SLIPPING') when an official extension has been granted OR exemptive-relief requests are pending; both conditions are satisfied here — one formal one-year extension was granted in Feb 2025, and SIFMA/IIB relief requests are publicly pending as of Aug 2026. No second extension has been announced, so score 2 is not warranted.

plan_financing.fact: Japan's 10-year JGB yield reached 3.000% on 1 September 2026 — its highest since 1996 — triggered by a record ¥143 trillion in FY2027 budget requests submitted on 31 August, with the Takaichi government declining to set spending ceilings for a new investment/national-security category; the 10y yield stood at ~2.9% on 7 September. However, the 30-year JGB auction on 3 September cleared with a bid-to-cover of 3.79 vs. a 12-month average of 3.52 (Bloomberg, 3 Sept 2026), and the 10-year auction on 1 September also reportedly cleared with robust demand (Universal Asset Owners, 1 Sept 2026). No emergency BOJ operation or failed auction (BTC <2) has been reported.
plan_financing.rationale: The 10-year yield has risen roughly +80 bps from ~2.1% in March to ~3.0% on fiscal-concern news, far exceeding the 25 bps UNCLEAR threshold and approaching the 50 bps DISORDERLY threshold; however, all recent auctions have cleared well above BTC 2 (30y BTC 3.79) with no failed auction or emergency BOJ operation, so the rubric's DISORDERLY criterion (failed auction or >50 bps spike in a single fiscal-news event) is not cleanly met, keeping the reading at UNCLEAR (1).

dissent.view: Universal Asset Owners / The Probability Desk (1 Sept 2026) characterises the 3% print as a 'term-premium event, not a fiscal crisis,' noting the same-day 10y auction cleared with robust demand, suggesting conditions are closer to 0 than 1.

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings posted 'U.S. Private Credit Default Rate Remains at Record High 6.0% in May 2026' on June 15 2026 (LSTA/Fitch commentary page). A secondary aggregator (angelinvestorsnetwork.com, ~Aug 2026) citing Fitch's own release states the TTM rate climbed to 6.1% for the period ending July 2026, and FinancialJuice (X, ~Aug 4 2026) confirms Fitch 'remains at record high in July 2026'. Fitch LinkedIn title (index 26) ambiguously reads 'drops to 5.2% in July' — not independently verifiable from the full release.
direct_lending_default.rationale: The Fitch PCDR (inclusive of distressed exchanges and LMEs) is confirmed at 6.0% through May 2026 and the most detailed secondary read puts July 2026 at 6.1%; applying the rubric's anchor-retention rule and the available corroborating evidence, 6.1% is the best single reading for the July 2026 period. A dissenting LinkedIn title from Fitch itself suggesting 5.2% in July is noted but unverifiable without the full release, warranting medium rather than high confidence.

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings data (cited by multiple sources, Aug 2026): 10 of 16 tracked non-traded BDCs breached quarterly redemption caps in Q2 2026. Named funds simultaneously gated in Q2: Blackstone BCRED (~$79B AUM, ~10% requests vs 5% cap), Apollo Debt Solutions BDC (~16.8% requests vs 5% cap), Morgan Stanley North Haven Private Income Fund ($7B, 11.6% vs 5% cap), Cliffwater CCLFX (~$31B, 17% vs 5% cap). Blue Owl OBDC II ($1.6B) permanently closed gates. Robert A. Stanger & Co. puts Q2 repurchase requests at 12.4% of NAV - highest on record - with only 38% fulfilled and ~$9.6B backlog. (Sources: ecmsource.com citing WSJ/Bloomberg/CNBC June 2026; angelinvestorsnetwork.com citing Fitch, Aug 2026; tradingmarketsignals.com citing Stanger, Aug 17 2026)
redemption_gates.rationale: 10 of 16 BDCs in the Fitch sample breached quarterly caps simultaneously in Q2 2026, with at least 4 named funds - including BCRED ($79B) alone exceeding the $100B combined AUM threshold - clearly meeting the WIDESPREAD criterion of >=3 largest funds gating in the same quarter with combined AUM well above $100B. No corroborating rate or repo stress is required by rubric for structural cap breaches, but MOVE index elevation and asset-manager equity drawdowns corroborate systemic pressure.

dissent.view: CLA Wealth Advisors (Mar 2026) and CAIA (Apr 2026) characterise the episode as funds 'operating as designed' within contractual limits - not a gating crisis but structural mechanics functioning normally; they note caps are contractual features, not emergency restrictions.
iCapital argues credit fundamentals remain sound and the redemption process is 'orderly', distinguishing elevated requests from systemic distress.

new_imf_programs.fact: Ethiopia remains in active default on its $1B Eurobond (original missed coupon Dec 2023); on June 29 2026 an agreement-in-principle with ~45% of holders was announced but the exchange is not yet executed (africasacountry.com, July 14 2026). Bangladesh formally requested a new IMF arrangement on June 3 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/06/03), but Board approval has not been confirmed. Pakistan's May 8 2026 IMF action was a 3rd-review disbursement under its existing EFF, not a new program (imf.org, May 8 2026). No additional new missed coupons or Board-approved new EM programs confirmed in the March-September 2026 window.
new_imf_programs.rationale: One sovereign (Ethiopia) is in confirmed active default/restructuring within or persisting into the trailing 6-month window; Bangladesh's program request is talk not action (no Board approval confirmed). One active distress event maps to RISING (band 1: 1-2 events).

dissent.view: Bangladesh's June 3 2026 formal IMF request could be counted as a new program initiation if the Board approves during the window, which would push the count toward 2 events, still RISING

china_ppi.fact: China PPI for industrial products increased by 3.5% year on year in July 2026, per NBS official English press release (stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260810_1965017.html), released 2026-08-10. Corroborated by Xinhua (2026-08-09) and SCIO (2026-08-10). August 2026 data not yet published (NBS typically releases ~10th of following month; today is 2026-09-07).
china_ppi.rationale: At +3.5% YoY, China PPI is in positive territory and represents a meaningful cost-push signal after a prolonged deflationary streak that ended in March 2026; the rubric scores on the SIZE of the move, and +3.5% is a moderate positive print flagging input-cost pressure exportable to global supply chains.

trade_actions.fact: At least 4 confirmed new major-economy trade measures against/by China in the trailing 3 months: (1) USTR new 12.5% Section 301 tariff on Chinese goods effective July 24, 2026 (China-Briefing/USTR, July 23, 2026); (2) EU definitive anti-dumping duty on Chinese polyamide yarns under Regulation 2026/1823, effective July 27, 2026; (3) China MOFCOM provisional anti-dumping deposits up to 54.3% on US and Mexican pecans, effective August 11, 2026 (Global Times); (4) China export controls on drones to US + ban on 6 US entities, August 5, 2026 (NBC News/AP). Additional: US DoC circumvention inquiry on China-origin spray-foam components (Federal Register, July 21, 2026).
trade_actions.rationale: Five distinct new measures (tariffs, anti-dumping duties, export controls) by major economies are confirmed within the trailing 3 months, well exceeding the rubric threshold of >=4 measures for ESCALATING (level 2). The 12.5% Section 301 tariff also constitutes a broad across-sector tariff round on Chinese goods, further satisfying the escalation criterion.

dissent.view: Xi-Trump summit (May 2026) and a structured bilateral adjustment phase post-summit suggest a managed framework reducing likelihood of full truce breakdown; some sources characterise measures as 'targeted' rather than broad escalation

license_flow.fact: China's core April 2025 rare-earth export licensing regime (covering seven medium/heavy REEs and downstream magnets containing Tb/Dy) remains fully in force under MOFCOM case-by-case licensing. General licences were issued in December 2025 to a handful of pre-cleared Chinese exporters (JL MAG, San Huan, Yunsheng) but are 'not broadly available.' Processing times run 45 working days by statute but 'routinely exceed 60–120 days' in practice for heavy-REE approvals. New 2026 catalogue entries added samarium, gadolinium, and lutetium compounds to the licensing list. The October 2025 Wave-2 expansion is suspended until 10 November 2026. Sources: blog.gettransport.com (July 7, 2026); rare-earth-mining.com (April 2026); certivo.com (March 2026); techtimes.com (May 27, 2026).
license_flow.rationale: The regime is case-by-case licensing for most exporters (general licences cover only a whitelist of three named producers), processing times far exceed 30 days (60–120 days reported), and new categories (samarium, gadolinium, lutetium) were added to the control list in the trailing three months relative to the as-of date — all of which maps squarely to rubric level 1 (SLOWING). Level 2 is not warranted because licences continue to be issued and there is no announced categorical denial or suspension of the licensing programme itself. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

dissent.view: Multi-institutional analysis cited by Rare Earth Exchanges reports licensing approval rates below 25% for European firms, implying near-categorical denial for some buyer segments — a potential level-2 read for EU-destination shipments.

truce_status.fact: The Nov-2025 US-China minerals truce (China's suspension of Oct-9-2025 rare earth export controls) remains formally in force until Nov 10, 2026 per MOFCOM Announcements 55-62 (Nov 7, 2025) and White House Fact Sheet (Nov 5, 2025). However, on June 22, 2026, China's MOFCOM added 10 US entities — including rare earth firms MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — to its export control list (dual-use ban), constituting a partial breach. As of 2026-09-07, ~64 days remain to the Nov 10, 2026 expiry with no confirmed renewal. Source: Benchmark Minerals/Bloomberg/Al Jazeera (June 22-25, 2026); Modern Diplomacy (Aug 21, 2026).
truce_status.rationale: Both rubric-1 triggers are met: (a) fewer than 90 days remain to the Nov 10, 2026 nominal expiry with no announced renewal, and (b) China's June 22, 2026 entity-list additions of MP Materials and USA Rare Earth constitute a partial breach. Score 2 is not warranted because the broad suspension is still formally operative and market signals (muted equity reaction, analysts calling the listings 'largely symbolic') do not corroborate full collapse.

dissent.view: FDD (June 24, 2026) argues the June 22 entity-list action 'ended the pause,' implying Score 2 (lapsed/controls reimposed); but this reads entity-specific dual-use restrictions as equivalent to full reimposition of broad export controls, which market prices and the formal MOFCOM suspension status do not support.

re_blacklist.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (issued 22 June 2026, effective immediately) named 10 specific US entities on China's export control list. The two US rare-earth producers explicitly listed are MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc. The full list: Aveox, Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, MP Materials Corp, and USA Rare Earth. The measure bans dual-use item exports to the named firms only. Multiple corroborating sources (Global Times citing MOFCOM directly, Bloomberg, Reuters via Al Jazeera, Benchmark Minerals, Arnold & Porter legal advisory) confirm the restriction is entity-specific. Market signal: MP Materials stock was roughly flat on announcement day and USA Rare Earth was modestly higher — consistent with a firm-specific, partially symbolic action rather than a sector-wide shock. Primary source: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026, https://english.mofcom.gov.cn; corroborated by https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202606/1364081.shtml and https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-22/china-places-two-us-rare-earths-producers-on-export-control-list
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) are on the MOFCOM export-control list as of 22 June 2026, satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific). Multiple sources explicitly confirm the restriction is firm-specific and does not constitute a blanket/sector-wide ban on US rare-earth producers as a class, ruling out level 2.

hree_premium.fact: Rare Earth Exchanges (Sept 3 2026, anchored to Aug 2026 CREIA data) states dysprosium and terbium cost 'up to 4x more outside China'; Argus data cited by Reuters (June 2026) puts the ex-China premium for dysprosium and terbium oxide at 'x4 to x5'; CTIA Aug 2026 official China avg: terbium oxide RMB 6,680/kg (~$920/kg), dysprosium oxide RMB 1,423/kg (~$196/kg); Platts CIF North America (Mar 31 2026): terbium $4,900/kg (~5.3x), dysprosium $1,200/kg (~6.3x); Benchmark Minerals (Mar 24 2026): 2025 avg dysprosium CIF North America was 4.4x EXW China.
hree_premium.rationale: Triangulating the most recent official Chinese price data (CTIA Aug 2026) against contemporaneous ex-China assessments (REEx Sept 2026, Argus/Reuters June 2026) yields a central ex-China HREE premium multiple of ~4-5x; 4.5 is the midpoint of the Argus x4-x5 range and consistent with the REEx 'up to 4x' floor, mapped directly to the rubric's multiple format.

genius_impl.fact: U.S. regulators missed the GENIUS Act statutory July 18, 2026 rulemaking deadline without issuing any final rules. As of that date, principal rule packages from the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury remained Notices of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRMs); several comment periods remained open past the deadline (e.g., a joint customer-identification rule open until Aug. 21, an FDIC AML proposal open until Aug. 4). No final rules had been published as of late August 2026. Source: The Block, July 18 2026 (https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-07-18-us-regulators-miss-genius-acts-one-year-deadline-for-final-stablecoin-rules-408843); crypto.news, ~Aug 2026 (https://crypto.news/genius-act-missed-deadline-regulators-writing-rules/); tech-insider.org, ~July 24 2026 (https://tech-insider.org/genius-act-stablecoin-law/).
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric scores 2 for 'deadline missed without final rules.' The July 18, 2026 statutory deadline passed with zero final rules published across all primary regulators (OCC, FDIC, NCUA, Federal Reserve, Treasury); all packages remain at NPRM stage with some comment periods still running into August 2026, satisfying the rubric's 'deadline missed without final rules' criterion unambiguously. The GENIUS Act's 18-month effective-date backstop (Jan 18, 2027) now governs, further confirming the rulemaking failure.

dissent.view: The missed deadline does not void the GENIUS Act or its Jan. 18, 2027 effective date; agencies are continuing to finalize rules on their own post-deadline timeline, and no court stay or compliance-failure event has occurred—some observers characterise this as a delay rather than a structural breakdown.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Four hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft) raised 2026 capex guidance to ~$725-760B (+77% YoY from ~$410B in 2025), with Amazon lifting to ~$220B and Alphabet to $195-205B at Q2 earnings. AI-attributable cloud revenue in Q2 2026 accelerated QoQ: Google Cloud +82% YoY to $24.8B (up from +63% in Q1), Azure +43% YoY (up from +40% in FY Q2), AWS +37% YoY to $42.23B; Microsoft AI annualized run rate $37B +123% YoY. Sources: Microsoft 8-K Jul 29 2026 (SEC); saasrise.com/news Aug 2026; valueaddvc.com Aug 2026; Financial Times via Yahoo Finance Apr 30 2026.
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~77% YoY) materially exceeds AI-cloud revenue growth rates (~37-82% YoY), keeping the gap WIDE; however, AI-attributable revenues are accelerating QoQ across all three major cloud segments - not decelerating - which disqualifies the WIDENING FAST (2) classification and firmly places this at rubric level 1.

dissent.view: Sequoia Capital (David Cahn, 2025 estimate) put the annual gap between AI infrastructure spend and AI ecosystem revenue at ~$600B; no 2026 update confirms narrowing - suggesting the gap may be worse than headline cloud growth rates imply when non-hyperscaler AI revenue is included

Moody's May 2026 forecast revision flagged explicit credit risk if 'strong profit growth from AI investments fails to materialise', implying ratings-agency concern that current revenue trajectory may not suffice - a more bearish reading than the rubric-1 classification

gpu_refi_stress.fact: On July 29 2026, CoreWeave (CRWV) CDS spread hit ~855 bps (implied ~50% five-year default probability); within days CoreWeave had to sweeten terms to place a $2.6B leveraged loan tied to its Anthropic relationship -- per Metir AI (Aug 2 2026) and TechTimes (Jul 30 2026). Separately, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and SMBC were actively seeking to offload AI data-center debt via Significant Risk Transfers (SRTs), per FT/Tech Newsday May 3-6 2026.
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: CoreWeave is a named borrower facing a demonstrated refinancing wall (had to sweeten a $2.6B deal) with CDS pricing at distressed levels, and major banks are offloading AI/data-center debt -- all squarely matching Rubric 1 SIGNS criteria. No confirmed outright default or distressed exchange has been reported, so Rubric 2 ACUTE is not warranted.

dissent.view: CoreWeave closed an $8.5B investment-grade-rated GPU-backed DDTL 4.0 facility (A3/Moody's, A-low/DBRS) on March 31 2026 and Q1 2026 revenue of $2.078B beat consensus by >5%, suggesting the primary market remained open to well-structured GPU-backed paper at near-investment-grade spreads.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: The Trepp CMBS office delinquency rate rose 103 basis points to an all-time high of 12.34 percent in January 2026, per Multi-Housing News citing Trepp data (published ~Feb 2026). The overall Trepp CMBS rate was 7.86% in July 2026 (the latest available month), but no Trepp office-sector-specific figure beyond January 2026 was retrievable from public sources.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The rubric requires the latest Trepp CMBS office delinquency percent; the most recent explicitly stated Trepp office figure found is 12.34% (January 2026). KBRA data (a dissenting source) shows the office rate at 13.9% in January 2026 and 12.8% in February 2026, suggesting Trepp and KBRA differ by methodology/universe, so the Trepp figure is used as the primary reading. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-01 data but the prior applied value was 2026-03 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: KBRA-rated CMBS office delinquency rate was 13.9% in January 2026, falling to 12.8% in February 2026 — higher than Trepp's 12.34% for the same period, reflecting a different rated universe and methodology.
S&P Global noted the CMBS office rate 'surpasses 10.5%' in January 2026 (paywalled headline figure, lower bound only).

regional_bank_stress.fact: Forbes Advisor (updated ~Aug 2026, drawing on FDIC data last refreshed Aug 21 2026) reports five US bank failures YTD 2026, including Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia (closed May 1 2026, <$10bn assets) which followed an FDIC enforcement action issued April 2026, and Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust (Jan 30 2026, $261M assets) which Bisnow documented had real-estate/CRE-linked loan exposure. At least 3-4 failures fall in the trailing 6-month window (Mar-Sep 2026), but explicit FDIC/Fed/OCC attribution of CRE concentration as a stated cause is confirmed for only 1-2 of those failures; no single failure exceeded $10bn assets and no coordinated interagency emergency facility was identified. Sources: https://www.forbes.com/advisor/banking/list-of-failed-banks/ ; https://www.fdic.gov/bank-failures/failed-bank-list (Aug 21 2026); https://www.bisnow.com/national/news/capital-markets/cre-tied-to-first-bank-failure-of-2026-133023
regional_bank_stress.rationale: The rubric's ISOLATED threshold (score=1) is satisfied by at least one public FDIC enforcement action in the trailing 6 months (April 2026 action preceding Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia closure) and 1-2 small-bank failures with documented or inferred CRE/real-estate exposure, each well below $10bn in assets. The CLUSTER threshold (score=2) is not met because explicit CRE attribution by regulators is confirmed for fewer than 3 failures and no single failure exceeded $10bn assets nor was a coordinated interagency emergency action identified.

dissent.view: Bankrate (as of Feb 2026) reported only 1 bank failure in 2026 (Metropolitan Capital), suggesting lower failure count if their data was not updated to reflect subsequent 2026 closures - however Forbes and FDIC data supersede this as more current.

govt_stability.fact: The Second Lecornu government (minority coalition: RE, MoDem, HOR, UDI) is incumbent since 10 Oct 2025. It invoked Article 49.3 to pass both the revenue and expenditure sections of the 2026 budget, surviving four separate no-confidence motions in Jan 2026 (highest tally: 269 vs. 288 required on 23 Jan 2026). Budget adopted 2 Feb 2026 after two further failed motions (260 vs. 289 required). Sources: Euronews 23 Jan 2026 (https://www.euronews.com/2026/01/23/french-government-avoids-collapse-after-surviving-two-no-confidence-votes), Al Jazeera 2 Feb 2026 (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/2/france-adopts-2026-budget-after-two-no-confidence-votes-fail), Wikipedia Second Lecornu government (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Lecornu_government).
govt_stability.rationale: The government holds no working majority and has repeatedly invoked Article 49.3 while surviving — not losing — multiple no-confidence votes; this maps precisely to Rubric Band 1 (FRAGILE). Band 2 is excluded because no confidence vote was passed and no dissolution or snap election was called.

rating_action.fact: Fitch cut France from AA- to A+ (stable outlook) in September 2025; S&P cut France from AA- to A+ (stable outlook) on 17 October 2025 (spglobal.com, france24.com); Moody's kept Aa3 but revised outlook to negative on 25 October 2025 (france24.com). Both Fitch and S&P downgrades are within the trailing 12 months. As of late August 2026 Fitch reaffirmed A+/stable and S&P reaffirmed A+/stable in May 2026; Moody's Aa3/negative remains in force.
rating_action.rationale: Rubric band 2 requires an actual rating cut in the trailing 12 months; both Fitch (Sep 2025) and S&P (Oct 17 2025) executed one-notch cuts from AA- to A+, each within 12 months of 2026-09-07. Moody's negative outlook (band 1) is also present but is subordinate to the confirmed downgrades.

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch Ratings subprime auto ABS 60+ day delinquency rate in June 2026 was 5.67%, down 64 bps year-over-year (Wolf Street, August 13 2026, citing Fitch Auto ABS Index). Peak was 6.90% in January 2026.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The Fitch Auto ABS Index is the primary institutional benchmark for subprime auto 60+ DPD; the June 2026 reading of 5.67% is the latest hard monthly figure available, representing a seasonal improvement from the January record but still materially elevated vs. historical norms. The rubric calls for the latest reported percent, which maps directly to 5.67.

dissent.view: Motley Fool (Sep 2, 2026) citing Fitch places Q2-end subprime at ~5.8% and notes July showed 'renewed deterioration,' implying the rate may have risen above 5.67% in July-August 2026 — but no hard July/August monthly figure was publicly confirmed.

Symend (updated Aug 31, 2026) and multiple sources anchor the January 2026 peak at 6.9% per Fitch, with narrative that Q2 improved but H2 2026 expected to re-weaken; no single competing monthly number for July-August confirmed.

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm 30+ DPD held flat at 2.8% YoY in Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026), per its shareholder letter; Klarna Pay Later 30+ DPD fell to 1.3% in Q1 2026 (down 30 bps QoQ) and POS installment 30+ DPD at 3.0% (down 20 bps), per Klarna Q2 2026 slides (Investing.com, ~Aug 2026). Richmond Fed (Feb 2026) cites industry charge-off rate of 1.83% for 2023, falling, with 'no clear evidence of elevated stress.'
bnpl_delinq.rationale: Affirm 30+ DPD is flat YoY at 2.8% (not up >100 bps), Klarna delinquency metrics are declining YoY/QoQ, and industry charge-offs remain well below 3%—squarely within the STABLE rubric (flat or down YoY, charge-offs contained). No named provider meets the RISING or SPIKING thresholds. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-Q1/Q2 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08-27 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: LendingTree March 2026 survey finds 47% of BNPL users self-reported a late payment in the past year, up from 41% in 2025—suggesting rising consumer strain not yet captured in hard delinquency series.

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (published June 30, 2026): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.' Source: https://data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20july%201
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric requires the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the IMF COFER official release for 2026Q1 gives exactly 57.13%, which is the load-bearing figure. This is the most recent published quarter (Q2 2026 data not yet released as of 2026-09-07) from the primary authoritative source.

dissent.view: coferdata.com displays USD at 56.77% for its 'latest quarter,' but the site acknowledges earlier quarters may include interpolated estimates and this figure does not match the official IMF Q1 2026 release.

weaponization_event.fact: As of April 2026 (IAI Brief 26|17, April 2026): EU chose 'joint borrowing over confiscation in December 2025,' leaving Russian sovereign assets (~€210bn) frozen but NOT seized. Separately, BRICS Pay began 'operational deployment in 2026' integrating CIPS/UPI/Pix/SPFS (economy.com.pk, Sep 2026; informedclearly.com, Jun 2026) and 'The Unit' gold-backed token moved into sandbox-testing phases, targeting full launch at the 2026 New Delhi BRICS summit.
weaponization_event.rationale: No new sovereign reserve seizure (ownership transfer) has been executed in 2026—the Russian freeze pre-dates the rubric window and full confiscation was explicitly rejected in Dec 2025, ruling out score 2. BRICS Pay operational deployment and 'The Unit' sandbox constitute new non-dollar settlement system launches/agreements with official backing, placing the indicator firmly at score 1 (TALK/early launch).

dissent.view: Some secondary sources (watcher.guru, informedclearly.com) claim BRICS Pay has 'gone live' and reduced USD intra-bloc trade by two-thirds, implying closer to operational action; but higher-authority sourcing (economy.com.pk, RBI statements) characterises this as technical integration still targeting the summit for full deployment, not a completed operational switch by a major economy.

insurer_exits.fact: NAIC Aug 5 2026 report ('Examining Homeowner Property Insurance Market Dynamics', MCAS 2018-2024) finds company-initiated non-renewal rates rose 96%-216% across ALL regional zones; Climate Cosmos (Jun 2026) enumerates 13 named states with active non-renewal/exit waves (CA, FL, LA, TX, GA, OK, CO and others); FL non-renewed 3.35% of policies (highest nationally), CA 3.18% (3.9x 2018 rate); NAIC simultaneously characterises the market as 'operationally strong overall' with improved 2024 underwriting and 715 active carriers; FL Citizens count fell to ~385K-395K by Jan 2026 (lowest since 2012), a partial stabilisation signal. No confirmed full exit by a top-10 insurer from a major state in 2026. Sources: content.naic.org Aug 5 2026; climatecosmos.com Jun 18 2026; leadgen-economy.com Jun 25 2026.
insurer_exits.rationale: Documented non-renewal waves span approximately 13 states across all NAIC regions, placing this squarely in the 5-15 state RISING band; the rubric threshold for ACCELERATING (>15 states or full top-10 insurer exit) is not clearly met, and NAIC's own characterisation of broad market operational strength plus FL stabilisation signals keep this out of the most severe tier.

cat_losses.fact: Swiss Re Institute reports global insured nat-cat losses of $42bn in H1 2026, 16% below the $66bn long-term H1 trend; Gallagher Re puts H1 at $46bn, 28% below its $64bn 10-year average; no single event exceeded $5bn insured in H1 2026 (Swiss Re / Gallagher Re / Aon, July 2026). No major hurricane landfall or >$10bn single event reported through early September 2026.
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses ($42-47bn) are materially below the 10-year H1 average ($64-66bn), satisfying neither the '>average' trigger for level 1 nor the '>150% of average' or '>$30bn single event' thresholds for level 2; no single event breached the $10bn threshold required for even level 1.

dissent.view: Aon estimates H1 2026 at $47bn (vs Swiss Re $42bn and Gallagher Re $46bn) - all still below average, direction consistent
Munich Re pegs H1 2026 at $44bn, also below long-term averages

ss_reform_news.fact: The 2026 Social Security Trustees Report (released June 9, 2026, SSA.gov/oact) projects the OASI Trust Fund depleted in Q4 2032 -- one quarter earlier than the 2025 report -- with the 75-year actuarial deficit widening to 4.42% of taxable payroll (up 16% from 3.82%). Combined OASDI depletion remains 2034. Multiple reform bills are actively debated in Congress (e.g., Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act H.R. 9187; PROMISE Act introduced July 14, 2026) but NO benefit cuts have been enacted or automatically triggered.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report materially worsened the OASI depletion date (2033 -> 2032) and widened the long-run funding gap, and reform is actively debated in Congress -- both conditions for band 1 (DEBATE). No automatic reduction has been triggered (depletion is still 6 years away) and no legislation enacting cuts has been signed into law, ruling out band 2 (CUTS).

dissent.view: CBO (Feb 2026) estimates the automatic cut upon 2032 depletion at ~28%, vs. the Trustees' 22%, reflecting different economic assumptions -- same depletion date but larger projected shortfall

pension_leverage_event.fact: TPR market oversight report (data to 31 March 2025) states: the LDI market has shrunk from ~£1.5 trillion (end-2021) to ~£0.7 trillion; daily volatility in leveraged LDI assets is more than 50% lower than at end-2021; LDI managers have raised rate buffers to ~300 bps (vs ~150 bps pre-2022); and 'LDI managers have maintained higher buffer thresholds, reducing leverage and improved collateral management.' No regulator alert, forced-selling episode, or central-bank intervention has been identified in 2026. Source: TPR, 'Market Oversight: How well pension schemes are prepared for LDI risk', thepensionsregulator.gov.uk (data to 31 March 2025). The most recent gilt-yield stress episode (Jan 2025, 30-yr gilt at 26-yr high) saw some cash calls but market advisers described it as 'orderly' with no forced selling — Reuters/MarketScreener, January 2025.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: Rubric level 0 requires LDI buffers adequate with no margin stress cited by TPR/ESMA. TPR's own market-oversight data confirm buffers at ~300 bps (above the 250 bps regulatory minimum), leverage materially reduced, and no forced-selling or regulator-flagged liquidity crisis in 2025-2026; the Jan-2025 gilt selloff produced orderly cash calls, not a blowup. No evidence of a 2026 episode elevating this to level 1 or 2.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): funded ratio of the 100 largest U.S. public pension plans was 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, down from 88.7% as of June 30, 2026. Source: Milliman / BusinessWire, published August 27, 2026 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827829119/en/Milliman-analysis-Public-pension-funded-ratio-slips-again-to-88.2-as-of-July-31).
funded_ratio.rationale: The rubric requests a representative large US public-pension funded ratio as a percent; the Milliman PPFI is the standard monthly benchmark for the 100 largest plans and its July 31, 2026 reading of 88.2% is the most recently published authoritative figure, mapping directly to the rubric's requested metric.

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' projects the national average funded ratio (253 statewide and municipal systems) at 85.0% for FY2026, up from 81.2% in FY2025 — a broader universe than the Milliman top-100 and based on actuarial (not market) valuation dates.

S&P Global Ratings (Jan 2026) estimated a sustainable funded ratio of ~81% for typical public-pension issuers based on FY2025 audit data (June 30, 2025 measurement), reflecting a longer actuarial lag.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (data through end of 2025, published July 1 2026): 'the median duration from IR to COD was over 5 years for projects built in 2025' - specifically reported as 61 months by LBNL, up from 36 months in 2015 and 22 months in 2008. Source: https://emp.lbl.gov/queues and https://emp.lbl.gov/publications/queued-2026-edition-characteristics
interconnection_months.rationale: LBNL's 2026 Edition directly reports 61 months as the median IR-to-COD wait for the 2025 cohort of completed projects, which is the primary published figure for this indicator. This maps mechanically to a value of 61 months per the rubric.

dissent.view: 45 months median IR-to-signed-IA (interconnection agreement, not COD) for 2025, per LBNL 2026 Edition - this is a shorter upstream milestone in the process, not the full queue duration

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Gov. Hochul signed Executive Order 62 on July 14, 2026, enacting the first U.S. statewide data center moratorium (50 MW+ facilities, 1-year DEC permitting hold). As of Sept 1, 2026, electricchoice.com tracks 321 moratoriums across 32 states (261 currently in force), with NJ (72), OH (35), MI (35), GA (28) leading local counts. datacenterbans.com (end-Aug 2026) identifies a second statewide pause: Texas PUC/ERCOT effective freeze on new grid connections while auditing ~200 GW of interconnection requests. DLA Piper (July 1, 2026) reports >100 local moratoria adopted nationwide and an estimated $64 billion in projects blocked or delayed.
dc_moratoria.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires a statewide moratorium enacted OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses: both conditions are met — New York EO 62 is an enacted statewide moratorium, Texas has a de facto statewide grid freeze, and 32 states with 261 active local restrictions far exceed the >10 threshold.

dissent.view: Axis Intelligence (Aug 9, 2026) logs only 10 verified formal restriction actions across 9 jurisdictions in its stricter verified-entry log, which would nominally fall at the rubric-1/2 boundary — but this tracker explicitly excludes many local pauses pending primary-source confirmation and is therefore an undercount relative to broader trackers.

ai_power_pressure.fact: DOE invoked Federal Power Act Section 202(c) emergency orders three times in 2026 — January (PJM Order 202-26-06 and ERCOT Order 202-26-01), May 18, and twice in July — authorizing PJM and ERCOT to curtail data-center and large-load backup generation as a last resort before declaring Energy Emergency Alerts, explicitly driven by data-center load growth outpacing grid capacity. In parallel, New York issued Executive Order 62 moratorium on DEC permits for facilities ≥50 MW and Texas imposed an effective freeze on new ERCOT grid connections pending audit of ~200 GW of interconnection requests. Sources: DOE energy.gov 202(c) orders (Jan 26 and May 18, 2026); datacenterbans.com (Aug 2026); spotlightpa.org (Jul 31, 2026); techtimes.com (Jul 4, 2026).
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Three confirmed DOE 202(c) emergency orders in 2026 authorizing curtailment of data-center load on PJM and ERCOT, plus statewide moratoriums in New York and Texas, satisfy the rubric's top band: confirmed curtailment authority exercised and power-scarcity-driven moratoria declared. PJM itself stated no data centers were actually forced onto backup generators (orders used as standby authority), but the rubric threshold is met by declared grid emergencies and moratoriums.

dissent.view: PJM stated as of July 31 that it had not actually implemented curtailment orders — no data centers were physically forced onto backup generators — suggesting the situation may still be closer to Band 1 in practice.
LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition shows total active U.S. queue volume fell 10% year-over-year through end-2025, potentially signaling early easing of generation-side pressure.

mine_disruptions.fact: As of early September 2026, at least three top-20 copper mines have confirmed, active production cuts: (1) Grasberg (world #2) running at ~65% capacity in H2 2026 after its Sep 2025 mudslide, with full restart pushed to early 2028 (mining.com, May 8 2026); (2) Kamoa-Kakula (top-5 globally) revised 2026 output down to 290,000-330,000 t from 420,000 t after 2025 seismic/flood event, with Q1 2026 output falling 54% YoY (Fastmarkets, Apr 20 2026); (3) Lundin Caserones cut 2026 guidance to 120,000-130,000 t from 130,000-140,000 t after back-to-back Chilean winter storm outages in July-Aug 2026, with a second storm on Aug 14 extending downtime (mining.com, ~Aug 2026). Additionally, Anglo American Los Pelambres, Antofagasta, and Codelco El Teniente/Andina all reported storm-related stoppages in July 2026 (CNBC Jul 31, mining.com Jul 18 2026). The ICSG cut its 2026 mine supply growth forecast to 1.6% from 2.3% citing DRC, Chile and Indonesia constraints including Grasberg and Kamoa (Oregon Group, May 2026), and Benchmark Minerals forecast a refined copper market deficit in 2026 due to Grasberg alone.
mine_disruptions.rationale: Three or more named top-20 mines (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Caserones) have confirmed active, measured production cuts in 2026, and institutions including Benchmark Minerals and ICSG have forecast a market deficit partly attributable to these disruptions — this maps squarely to rubric level 2 (CLUSTER: >=3 major mines disrupted, OR lost output large enough that institutions forecast a market deficit).

dissent.view: Goldman Sachs maintained a 2026 copper surplus forecast as of mid-2026, diverging from Benchmark Minerals' deficit call, though both agree on the scale of individual mine losses.

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 Copper Market Forecast projects a refined copper market SURPLUS of ~96,000 metric tons in 2026, reversing its prior October 2025 deficit forecast of -150,000 mt, driven by weaker demand growth (1.6% vs prior 2.1%) and stronger secondary/scrap output. Source: ICSG Copper Market Forecast 2026/2027 (April 2026), as reported by ADMIS (April 24 2026), RecyclingToday (April 28 2026), IndexBox (April 25 2026), and Metalnomist (July 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: A forecast surplus of +96,000 mt is unambiguously positive and well outside the ±100kt balanced band, mapping directly to rubric band 0 (SURPLUS). The April 2026 ICSG update is the most authoritative and most recent official forecast available.

dissent.view: ICSG October 2025 forecast projected a refined copper DEFICIT of -150,000 mt for 2026 (score=2), since superseded by the April 2026 revision
J.P. Morgan projected a -330,000 mt deficit for 2026, driven by AI/hyperscale data center demand (score=2)

drought_chip_farm.fact: As of Aug 18-Sep 1 2026, ~30% of the Intermountain West (AZ, CO, NM, UT, WY) is in Extreme (D3) or Exceptional (D4) drought per the U.S. Drought Monitor; Arizona ADWR confirms D3/D4 long-term drought in every county; NIFC Sep 1 2026 outlook lists exceptional drought (D4) in portions of Nevada, New Mexico, Colorado and Oregon. Source: drought.gov Intermountain West Drought Status Update Aug 20 2026 (https://www.drought.gov/drought-status-updates/drought-status-update-intermountain-west-2026-08-20) and NIFC Sep 1 2026 outlook (https://www.nifc.gov/nicc-files/predictive/outlooks/monthly_seasonal_outlook.pdf).
drought_chip_farm.rationale: D3 and D4 classifications are confirmed across major US Southwest farming and chip-fab water-supply regions (AZ, NV, NM), which satisfies the rubric's 'extreme/exceptional (D3-D4)' threshold for level 2. No confirmed fab production curtailment or water-rationing order at a specific chip fab was found for 2026, but D3-D4 alone is sufficient per the rubric; confidence is medium rather than high because the most granular Arizona/Nevada chip-fab-specific water data was not directly pulled from droughtmonitor.unl.edu in this session.

dissent.view: Monsoon rains brought some drought relief to portions of AZ, UT, and western CO in July-August 2026, and drought improved in parts of the Southwest per NIFC Sep 1 outlook, suggesting D3/D4 footprint may be shrinking locally

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,038.86 ft, storage 6,899,410 acre-feet = 26.4% of 26,120,000 AF capacity, per U.S. Bureau of Reclamation gauge data (reservoirbench.com citing USBR RISE, Sep 3 2026); all-time record low of 1,038.82 ft set Sep 1 2026; the 1,035-ft Hoover Dam minimum power-pool threshold is only ~3.9 ft below current surface.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.4% of capacity the reservoir is well below the rubric's <30% CRITICAL threshold; current elevation is also within 4 feet of the 1,035-ft power-generation operational threshold (rubric: within 15 ft), both criteria independently satisfy level 2. Physical impact is confirmed: USBR has flagged up to 40% additional reduction in Hoover Dam hydropower capacity and documented boat-ramp closures.

dissent.view: lakelevelnow.com reports 24% full as of Sep 4 2026 (slightly lower than reservoirbench 26.4%), likely reflecting a different capacity basis or rounding; directionally identical, both well below 30%.

water_dispute.fact: India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in April 2025 and physically cut Chenab flows via the Baglihar Dam (May 2025). On Aug 31 2026, a Permanent Court of Arbitration panel ruled the treaty 'remains fully in force' and India's abeyance 'not permissible'; India rejected the ruling on Sept 1 2026 (Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CNBC, Sept 1-3 2026). Pakistan's defence minister warned in June 2026 that water security could trigger war. Pakistan has logged 'abnormal, abrupt flow variations on the Chenab' (CNBC, June 22 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: A deliberate flow cut-off was physically carried out (Baglihar Dam, May 2025), the 65-year treaty remains formally suspended/rejected despite an international tribunal ruling it still binding, and a cabinet-level war threat tied directly to dam/river management was issued in June 2026 — all three rubric-2 triggers are met for the Indus dispute.

dissent.view: India cannot fully block Indus flows to Pakistan due to infrastructure limits; actual diversion is temporary and partial, not a permanent cut-off — CSIS argues the treaty suspension is legally contested but physical interdiction capacity is limited
On the Nile/GERD front, diplomacy is 'frozen' but no armed clash has occurred; GERD dispute rates TENSE (1) in isolation — New Arab, March 2026

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 1.9% from revised July level (131.1) and 2.5% from a year ago, reaching its highest level since end-2022. Source: FAO newsroom, https://www.fao.org/newsroom/detail/supply-concerns-drive-fao-food-price-index-higher/en, released 4 September 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM gain of +1.9% is below the 5% SPIKING threshold; the 3-month rise (June 130.3 to August 133.3) is ~2.3%, well below the 10% SPIKING threshold; index is rising both MoM and YoY, placing it squarely in ELEVATED (1).

china_export_curbs.fact: NDRC suspended phosphate (DAP/MAP) exports through August 2026 (imposed Dec 2025, extended Mar 2026 to N-K blends); urea export quotas (~3 Mt total 2026) reopened May 26 2026 with a first-ever NDRC-mandated FOB price floor of $660/t prilled and $670/t granular, per Profercy/keyuanfertilizer citing NDRC, May 26 2026. Phosphate ban was 'at least through August 2026' per FertilizerDaily July 29 2026; no confirmed post-August extension or full lifting found as of search date.
china_export_curbs.rationale: The NDRC price-floor system on urea (May 26, within trailing 3 months) is a NEW broadened restriction mechanism never previously used, qualifying as a tightening under the rubric; simultaneously the phosphate DAP/MAP ban remained in force through August 2026 and CoBank (Aug 2026) flagged high sulfur prices may force further extension, indicating the regime has not been lifted. Both the novel price-floor instrument and continued phosphate suspension map to rubric level 2 (NEW or broadened restriction in trailing 3 months).

dissent.view: Phosphate ban scheduled to expire August 31 2026 per original NDRC suspension timeline; no confirmed post-August extension found, which could argue the phosphate component reverted to level 1 (in-place quota) after Aug 31
CoBank (Aug 2026) flags possible extension of phosphate ban due to high sulfur prices but treats it as a risk/forecast, not a confirmed new restriction

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: straits.live (updated 6 Sep 2026): 'Effectively no, it is closed to commercial shipping as of 6 September 2026. 6 ships transited on August 30 vs ~85/day normal. Brent $96.28.' The June 2026 MOU collapsed in early July after attacks on commercial vessels; IRGC ballistic missile attacks on US convoy assets reported 5 Sep 2026; WTO/AIS data show fertilizer-related outbound shipments near zero since late February.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: The strait is effectively closed (transit ~7% of baseline), the June ceasefire/MOU has broken down with active military exchange ongoing, and Brent crude at ~$96/bbl confirms the closure signal - all three rubric conditions for rating 2 are satisfied. Naval convoys remain under active attack, so the 'convoys moving' cap to 1 does not apply given the collapsed truce and elevated oil price.

dissent.view: Some US military/JMIC counts log ~22 US-facilitated vessel transits/day (1-2 Sep), suggesting partial convoy flow continues, which could support a rating of 1

taiwan_tension.fact: ISW/AEI China & Taiwan Update (Sep 1 & Sep 4, 2026) reports Taiwan's Coast Guard Agency logged 244 PRC vessels in Taiwanese waters in July 2026 — a record high — and 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days of August 2026, roughly 60% coast guard ships, as part of persistent PRC patrols that began in May 2026; a two-day PLA live-fire drill was conducted in the Taiwan Strait on 24-25 July 2026 (SCMP, Jul 23 2026). No kinetic clash or blockade has been reported. Xi Jinping was engaged in diplomatic travel (SCO summit, Aug 31-Sep 1), not mobilization. Sources: https://www.aei.org/commentary/china-taiwan-update-september-1-2026/ ; https://www.aei.org/commentary/china-taiwan-update-september-4-2026/ ; https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3361554/pla-conducts-2-days-live-fire-drills-taiwan-strait-fujian-island
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent record-high PRC vessel presence and a recent live-fire drill in the Strait qualify as assertive/elevated pressure (Rubric 1), but there is no kinetic clash, formal blockade, or full mobilization signal, so Rubric 2 is not met.

dissent.view: armedconflicts.org characterizes the situation as 'Elevated intensity' standoff as of Sep 4 2026, consistent with Rubric 1 but using slightly stronger language

export_controls.fact: In the trailing 3 months: (1) US/allied side — MATCH Act debated in Congress (would blanket-ban all ASML immersion DUV exports to China), BIS added 52 Chinese entities to Entity List (July 2026, CNC/adjacent-tech category), US Commerce Secretary accused ASML of circumventing controls (June 2026). (2) China retaliation — MOFCOM on June 22 tightened dual-use export restrictions on 10 US companies; on July 24 added 14 EU entities to China Export Control List (MOFCOM Announcement No. 30); on August 5 announced countermeasures including strengthened UAV dual-use export controls to US and placed 6 US entities on countermeasure list; State Council Order No. 834 (April 7) created unified supply-chain legal framework enabling retaliatory action. Sources: substack.steptoe.com (Aug 10 2026), geopolitechs.org (Jul 24 2026), modeldiplomat.com (Jul 22 2026), nltimes.nl (Jun 24 2026), globaltimes.cn (Aug 5 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both the US/allied side (Entity List additions, MATCH Act pressure, ASML circumvention accusations) and China (MOFCOM Announcement No. 30, August 5 countermeasure package, 50% domestic procurement mandate) enacted new active measures within the trailing 3 months; China's MOFCOM actions constitute explicit counter-controls against US and allied entities, satisfying the rubric's level-2 threshold of target-country countermeasures.

dissent.view: The Busan truce (Oct 2025) suspended the BIS Affiliates Rule and China's Oct 9 extraterritorial measures through Nov 2026, and BIS Entity List additions in July 2026 clustered in CNC/adjacent categories rather than core semiconductor SME — suggesting the semiconductor-specific escalation track remains partially restrained by the truce framework. This could support a read of level 1 (tightening) rather than full level 2 retaliation specifically on semiconductors.

fab_concentration.fact: As of September 2026, all TSMC leading-edge (<=3nm) capacity is 100% in Taiwan: 3nm at ~180,000 wpm and 2nm ramping to ~100,000 wpm, both exclusively at Taiwan fabs (Fab 18, Fab 20, Fab 22). Arizona Fab 21 Phase 2 (3nm) is in equipment-installation phase with mass production targeted 2H 2027; Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm) targets 2028. Taiwan MoEA projects sub-5nm remains ~85% Taiwan through 2030. Source: TSMC 2025 Annual Report (investor.tsmc.com); TrendForce April 27 2026 (trendforce.com/news/2026/04/27); TrendForce Feb 6 2026 (trendforce.com/news/2026/02/06).
fab_concentration.rationale: Zero operational overseas <=3nm fab exists today and 100% of such capacity sits in Taiwan, placing this squarely in the EXTREME band (<10% outside Taiwan AND no operational overseas leading-edge fab). The Arizona and Kumamoto 3nm fabs are real but future-dated (2027-2028), so no market volume signal supports any current overseas share.

dissent.view: TSMC plans project ~20% of total (all-node) overseas capacity by 2028 and ~15% of sub-5nm in the US by 2030, and Arizona 3nm production is accelerated vs. original 2028 schedule, suggesting the EXTREME rating may be short-lived
TSMC long-term plan targets ~30% of advanced output in the US across six Arizona fabs, framing current concentration as transitional rather than structural

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: straits.live (updated 6 Sep 2026, citing PortWatch) recorded 6 Strait of Hormuz transits on 2026-08-30 vs. a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day (~7% of normal); UANI (Sep 3, 2026) reports 'security situation remains highly volatile' with Iran actively targeting commercial shipping; Brent crude at $97.39/bbl on Sep 7 (TradingEconomics), up ~47% year-on-year, corroborating severe supply disruption. The June 2026 MoU-driven reopening collapsed after IRGC resumed strikes on Jul 7; no functioning commercial convoy workaround is in operation.
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: At ~7% of pre-crisis transit volume with active Iranian military strikes on commercial vessels, no operational convoy regime, and Brent at ~$97/bbl (~47% above year-prior levels), all three rubric conditions for a '2=CLOSED' rating are met: volume well below 25% of normal, no convoy workaround, and a corroborating oil price signal consistent with closure.

dissent.view: JMIC cumulative count of 877 transits since the June 18 MoU could imply residual commercial throughput and a 'contested' reading, particularly given that some Iranian- and Chinese-linked vessels continue to move

Houthi Red Sea threats described as potential expansion rather than confirmed full closure; Security Council Report (Jul 2026) notes no Houthi maritime attacks since June 14 MoU, suggesting Red Sea may be separately rated as contested rather than closed

cable_incidents.fact: The PEACE subsea cable suffered a confirmed cut in the Red Sea, located ~1,450 km from Zafarana, Egypt, with repair expected to take several months due to cable ship capacity crunch; cause unknown. Source: Data Centre Dynamics, July 27, 2026 (https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/peace-subsea-cable-cut-in-the-red-sea-repair-to-take-months/).
cable_incidents.rationale: A named major cable (PEACE) is confirmed severed and unrepaired as of the most recent authoritative report (July 2026), with multi-month restoration timeline — satisfying rubric level 2. No market or connectivity signal found contradicting the outage, consistent with prior Red Sea cut patterns where rerouting partially masks but does not eliminate the disruption.

dissent.view: No evidence of a Hormuz cable being cut; AGBI (April 2026) and CNN (May 2026) describe Hormuz cables as at elevated threat only, not severed — pointing to rubric 1 for that sub-region.
Baltic Sea incidents (shadow fleet, through Dec 2025) have not yielded a confirmed current unrepaired cut as of Sep 2026; EU repair initiative underway, suggesting prior cuts were resolved.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: DTCC/FICC survey (July 27, 2026) found >$1.2T of Treasury cash activity already clearing at FICC with ~$300-400B still to onboard, and 79% of GSD netting members have account setups in place; simultaneously, as of Aug 7, 2026, the SEC had multiple pending exemptive-relief requests unresolved (SIFMA inter-affiliate, IIB cross-border, and 15c3-3 omnibus-margin relief with comment period closing Aug 31, 2026), and TBAC Q2 2026 (May 2026) identified documentation/legal-agreement backlogs as the 'largest challenge.' No deadline extension has been announced. Sources: DTCC/Finadium July 27 2026 (https://finadium.com/ficc-survey-shows-ust-clearing-at-scale-ahead-of-sec-deadline/); SEC Commissioner Uyeda statement Aug 7 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/uyeda-statement-update-secs-work-toward-treasury-clearing-implementation-080726-update-secs-work-toward-treasury-clearing-implementation-august-2026); TBAC Charge Q2 2026 May 2026 (https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/TBACCharge1Q22026.pdf).
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: The rubric scores 1=FRICTION when there is a documentation backlog or pending exemptive relief: both conditions are confirmed simultaneously — TBAC/TBACC cite ongoing legal-agreement backlogs and multiple SEC exemptive-relief requests (inter-affiliate, cross-border, omnibus margin) remain open as of early September 2026. No deadline extension (which would trigger score 2) has been announced, and DTCC reports strong infrastructure progress with 79% account readiness, ruling out score 0. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-08-07 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: DTCC president Brian Steele stated the industry is 'well positioned for the Treasury cash clearing deadline on December 31, 2026,' suggesting closer to SMOOTH (0); $1.2T already clearing indicates substantial completion.
